items.title: Google's Discover Core Update Finishes Rolling Out
items.summary: Google's February Discover core update, the first publicly labeled as such, finished rolling out on February 27 after 22 days, starting February 5, with goals to increase local relevance, reduce clickbait, and prioritize in-depth original content from expert sites, initially for US English users and expanding later. Early data shows increased regional personalization, fewer domains in top placements, and more topic variety but narrower publisher diversity. Publishers should wait at least a week post-update to assess performance via Search Console, focusing on regional and topical authority.

items.title: Google AI Overviews Surges Across 9 Industries
items.summary: Google AI Overviews (AIO) has surged 58% year-over-year from February 2025 to February 2026, now triggering on nearly half of all search queries across nine industries including healthcare, education, B2B tech, and restaurants. This growth reshapes SEO by showing that AIO citations overlap with only about 17% of top 10 organic rankings due to Google's FastSearch method. Content must be optimized for conversational queries and indexed content beyond traditional page-one performance.

items.title: Google AI Overview Citations From Top-Ranking Pages Drop Sharply
items.summary: Ahrefs' analysis shows only 38% of cited pages in AI Overviews rank in Google's top 10, down from 76%, with citations increasingly from positions 11–100 and beyond, due to improved parsing and query fan-out. YouTube accounts for 18.2% of citations outside top 100, highlighting video's role. Optimize for broad topic coverage across formats rather than single-keyword rankings.

items.title: Google Clarifies How It Picks Thumbnails For Search, Discover
items.summary: Google updated its Image SEO best practices to allow publishers to specify preferred thumbnails using schema.org markup or og:image meta tag. Large, high-resolution images without text are favored for better engagement in Search and Discover. Review markup to improve visibility.

items.title: Content marketing in an AI era: From SEO volume to brand fame
items.summary: In the AI era, informational SEO is collapsing as AI provides direct answers, shifting focus from traffic to brand fame via mental availability, distinctiveness, and emotional associations. Prioritize originality like proprietary research and active distribution over search pull. Audit content, invest in creative depth, and measure brand awareness.

items.title: How To Do Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) for Ecommerce
items.summary: AEO extends SEO and GEO for ecommerce by ensuring structured product data to improve AI representation and prevent hallucinations. Conduct content audits, create pillar pages with clusters, and track AI citations. Builds on SEO principles for broader visibility.

items.title: Literary agents urge writers to avoid AI as they see ‘change in nature of submissions’
items.summary: Literary agents are advising writers to steer clear of artificial intelligence in their submissions, observing a noticeable change in the nature of manuscripts received. Agencies have updated guidelines to reject works created or edited with generative AI, concerned that it suppresses authentic author voices. This reflects broader industry worries about AI-generated content flooding submissions.

items.title: Media Do Agrees to Buy Seven Seas
items.summary: Media Do International has agreed to acquire Seven Seas Entertainment, a leading independent English-language manga publisher, for $80 million, with the deal closing later in March 2026. Seven Seas, founded in 2004 by Jason DeAnglis, reported $50.4 million in 2024 sales and will maintain its leadership, editorial standards, and schedules post-acquisition. The move consolidates Media Do's position in digital distribution and manga publishing.

items.title: With New Owner, Tyrant Books Plans to Resume Publishing
items.summary: Tyrant Books, dormant since founder Giancarlo DiTrapano's passing, is resuming operations after author Luke Goebel acquired 50% ownership, partnering with Matthew Johnson of Fat Possum Records. Goebel, a former unpaid assistant, will lead editorial expansion while preserving the press's independent, risky literary focus. The backlist includes 23 titles, many adapted into films, with future distribution via Consortium.

items.title: From Traitors To TikTok Influencers: The Age Of The 'Quiet Author' Is Over
items.summary: Harriet Tyce saw a 96% sales boost after appearing as a Traitor on BBC's The Traitors, leveraging her thriller background for her new novel Witch Trial about a modern witch hunt. The piece discusses how BookTok, with over 370 billion views, has propelled authors like Colleen Hoover and self-published Cassie Steward to bestseller status via viral promotion. Platforms like TikTok are transforming quiet authors into public influencers.

items.title: HATER FRIDAY | Mass-Generating Literary Slop: AI-Written Books
items.summary: The opinion piece slams author Coral Hart for using AI tools like ChatGPT to produce over 200 romance novels in 2025, including repetitive titles like Mistletoe and Memorandums featuring clichéd plots. Hart earned six figures and sells AI writing courses via Plotprose, as revealed in a New York Times interview. Critics argue AI fails to capture human emotion, flooding markets with low-quality 'slop.'

items.title: Not Simon & Schuster: Deconstructing an Impersonation Scam
items.summary: Writer Beware's Victoria Strauss exposed a scam email impersonating Simon & Schuster, offering a $500,000 advance on a manuscript before demanding payments for fake self-publishing services. The likely AI-generated fraud from Nigeria used pressure tactics and wire transfers to extract $200-$15,000. It preys on authors seeking traditional deals amid industry vulnerabilities.

items.title: ‘Sinners’ Wins Top Prize at 2026 Actor Awards
items.summary: At the 32nd Annual Actor Awards presented by SAG-AFTRA on March 2, the film 'Sinners' triumphed with Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture, marking director Ryan Coogler's second such win, while Michael B. Jordan claimed Outstanding Lead Actor for his dual roles, upsetting Timothée Chalamet. Amy Madigan won Supporting Female Actor for 'Weapons,' and Jessie Buckley took Lead Actress for 'Hamnet.' The event highlighted major wins and snubs in the lead-up to the Oscars.

items.title: Disney Under Fire for ‘Captain Durag’ Cartoon Character
items.summary: Disney's 'Hey AJ!' introduced Captain Durag, a Black superhero whose durag serves as cape and mask to fight grime, sparking backlash on social media for being stereotypical and tone-deaf despite creation by a Black woman, Camille Corbett. Corbett defended it as celebrating Black culture, while viewers called it an 'abomination' and pushed for removal. The character debuted on January 15 but gained recent traction amid criticism.

items.title: ‘A Knight of Seven Kingdoms’ Actress Addresses Racial Backlash
items.summary: Tanzyn Crawford, playing Tanselle in HBO's 'A Knight of Seven Kingdoms,' responded to online racial backlash about her casting, noting George R.R. Martin confirmed she fit his vision and emphasizing the character's confidence. Despite some social media gripes labeling the series 'non-woke,' the show's first season received broadly positive fan reactions. Crawford described stepping into the Game of Thrones universe as intimidating but fulfilling.

items.title: Woke ‘Star Trek: Starfleet Academy’ Suffers Ratings Plunge
items.summary: Paramount+'s 'Star Trek: Starfleet Academy' faced audience backlash for left-wing lectures, poor writing, and elements like a male Klingon in a dress, leading to its quick drop from the Top 10 streaming charts. Fans on social media called it unwatchable, predicting cancellation after one season despite critic praise. The show's recent episodes highlighted ongoing dissatisfaction with its direction.

items.title: ‘Scream 7’ Sets Box Office Records Despite Boycott Calls
items.summary: Scream 7 achieved a franchise-record $97.2 million global opening, including strong previews, defying boycotts linked to Melissa Barrera's 2023 firing over pro-Palestine posts. Protests from groups like BDS failed to impact ticket sales, with audiences driving success amid ongoing controversy. The film's performance underscores resilience against organized backlash.

items.title: Anna Camp Deletes ‘Scream 7’ Post Mocking Boycott
items.summary: Scream 7 star Anna Camp deleted an Instagram story reposting 'The Boycott Didn't Work' amid the film's box-office success, apologizing for any harm intended toward fans upset over Melissa Barrera's firing. The post taunted boycott efforts tied to Barrera's pro-Palestine comments, sparking backlash. Camp clarified she meant no offense, as the film grossed over $64 million domestically.

items.title: Rowan Launches AI-Powered Platform to Address Small Business Succession Crisis
items.summary: Rowan is a new AI-powered succession platform designed to help small business owners prepare for successful transitions by addressing common preparation issues that lead to undervalued sales. It combines expert guidance with proprietary AI tools to organize financial and operational data, reduce owner dependence, modernize operations, improve cash flow, and attract buyers. Key features include a 360 business assessment, salability score, AI-driven Collect Agent for accounts receivable automation, which has recovered over $300,000 for clients, leading to sales boosts like $3.8 million above valuation.

items.title: How small businesses can win in the AI era
items.summary: Small businesses can leverage AI to enhance early customer discovery and build trust by emphasizing clarity, responsiveness, and human connection, as AI speeds up idea generation but customers prioritize authentic signals like reviews. Strategies include using AI for administrative tasks to free time for expertise, optimizing digital presence for AI visibility, and prioritizing speed with personalization. Tools highlighted involve AI for streamlining leads in WeddingPro and The Knot integration in ChatGPT.

items.title: Is AI Coming for Small Business? How Small Businesses are Approaching AI Integration
items.summary: Small businesses are rapidly adopting AI, with generative AI usage jumping from 23% in 2023 to 58% in 2025, using it for data analytics in email sorting, personalized marketing, and route optimization despite challenges like tech needs. No headcount reductions reported by 98% of leaders, with AI enhancing agility and decisions. Recommendations focus on automating workflows while preserving human elements like empathy in service.
